title: The rightward allocation pass
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,n,B\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n+1\le B$, and fix a schedule-alphabet input, a base configuration, an input-head position, an integer budget-head position, a budget tape, and a natural unary tape with $B$ markers. Starting in layout-right phase $0$ with unary head at $1$ and guide head at $0$ on the partial guide with $n+1$ copied cells, after $3B+2$ steps the machine is in layout-return phase $0$ with unary head at $B$ and guide head at $3B$, and its guide tape is the right guide of radius $3B$; the other configuration data is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a schedule-alphabet input, base configuration, and input-head position
integer budget-head position and budget tape
initial guide head is at $0$ on the partial guide with $n+1$ copied cells
replaced:
Let $n + 1 \le B$.  From the first rightward layout phase with unary head at cell $1$
over the unary tape with $B$ markers and guide head at cell $0$ over the partial guide
with $n+1$ copied cells, exactly $3B + 2$ steps reach radius $3B$, install the right
outer boundary marker, and enter the first layout-return phase with unary head at $B$,
guide head at $3B$, and guide tape the right guide of radius $3B$.
